text.p: Australian wine maker Brian McGuigan Wines Ltd said on Thursday the outlook for trading in the current year was very positive with the company budgeting for a healthy increase in net profit after tax.
"Results for the first quarter are broadly in line with that budget," chairman David Clarke said in a statement.

"The very good results so far this year have been primarily driven by the company's export performance where sales are up 135 percent compared to the corresponding period last year and 34 percent up on budget," Clarke said.
BRL Hardy managing director Stephen Millar said in a separate statement the agreement had given his company its first meaningful presence in the Hunter Valley region of New South Wales.
Millar said this would add to the company's operations in Victoria, South Australia, Western Australia and France.
